decisions.reason: As a design-led decorative line close to the core business but with no visible later evidence of continued promotion, it likely falls below aspiration more easily than a staple item and management would reallocate resources despite some slack.

This transparent burnout decorative fabric is a relatively style-sensitive extension of the existing offer, so if post-launch results were merely uncertain rather than clearly satisfactory, boundedly rational management would be inclined to discontinue it.

Because this burnout decorative fabric appears narrower than the multi-model lines and offers less scope to absorb weak demand, it is the kind of product a medium textile firm would drop when performance does not clearly meet aspiration.

A velour-like upholstery fabric fits the firm’s established upholstery competence and reorder-oriented service model, so with industry growth and some organisational slack management is more likely to keep it unless results are clearly poor.
The flame-retardant plain inbetween fabric is a functional, service-supporting product that suits dependable supply and continuity, making it more likely to meet aspiration and be retained.

A polyester lining fabric with satin sheen complements the firm’s sewing and sample-making capabilities and resembles a staple assortment item, so management would tend to keep it absent strong evidence of underperformance.
